subject.title: Feature: configPatch in plugin manifest — automatic config setup on install

question: Should OpenClaw add manifest-declared install-time config intent for third-party plugins, and what allowed paths, confirmation, conflict/array behavior, provenance, and uninstall guidance are required?
rationale: This changes a plugin install from enabling a package to letting package metadata mutate user configuration, which crosses product, upgrade-safety, and security boundaries that code inspection cannot decide alone.

options.title: Define guarded config intent
options.body: Approve a narrow manifest contract that validates against current config, shows a diff with a skip path, records provenance, and limits or classifies sensitive paths before writing.

options.title: Reject install-time mutation
options.body: Keep plugin install limited to plugin state and require setup/auth/doctor flows or manual config patch commands for broader config changes.

options.title: Defer to ClawHub/package policy
options.body: Require ClawHub/package trust metadata or a plugin setup flow to carry any install-time config request before core accepts it.

recommendation.title: Define guarded config intent
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow manifest contract that validates against current config, shows a diff with a skip path, records provenance, and limits or classifies sensitive paths before writing.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent live path history points most strongly to plugin manifest/install implementation ownership across the central files.
